paths.description: Homepage: entry, national forecast, navigation, consent, search and global UI template.
Rome city forecast: primary detail archetype and successful location-search destination.
News listing: content index/navigation archetype; represents category listings.
Current weather article: editorial detail, metadata and long-form reading archetype.
Primary location-search journey: Roma succeeds; an unknown query was exercised for recovery behavior.
Representative unknown route: verifies HTTP 404 and recovery page.

findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode evaluate probe reports matchMedia=true, html color-scheme “normal”, body background rgb(255,255,255), and no dark-theme CSS; the dark screenshot remains light.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven surface/text tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: High-contrast preferences have no authored adaptation.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no prefers-contrast or forced-colors rules; Lighthouse also identified multiple contrast failures, including the search placeholder at 2.32:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast adaptations, use system colors for controls, and verify all essential text and focus indicators.

findings.summary: Route and state changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: Rendered CSS inspection found no view-transition rules or names across the multi-page navigation surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Use cross-document View Transitions for eligible navigations with a no-motion fallback.

findings.summary: A full-screen consent wall obscures every representative page on first load.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show the modal covering the forecast/article before any interaction; on mobile it consumes virtually the full viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the blocking wall with a compact, equally weighted, readily dismissible consent surface that leaves core content visible.

findings.summary: Modal UI is implemented as custom role=dialog markup instead of the platform dialog primitive.
findings.evidence: DOM inspection found 0 <dialog> and 4 role=dialog elements, with no popover or details primitives.
findings.suggestedFix: Use <dialog> for modal consent/settings flows and native close/focus semantics; use popover/details for transient disclosure.

findings.summary: Dense chrome, carousels and secondary modules compete with the forecast.
findings.evidence: The desktop listing screenshot and homepage DOM show extensive navigation, news carousels, social controls and repeated modules before/around the primary forecast.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce repeated chrome, defer secondary news/ad modules, and make the current forecast the dominant viewport content.

findings.summary: The homepage overflows horizontally on a 360px viewport.
findings.evidence: The layout primitive measured scrollWidth 435 versus visual viewport 360, a 75px horizontal overflow, despite a viewport meta tag.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove fixed/minimum widths, use intrinsic sizing and minmax/clamp, and test at 320–400px without horizontal overflow.

findings.summary: Reusable forecast/news components rely on viewport layout rather than container responsiveness.
findings.evidence: Live CSS inspection found no @container or container-type declarations; the homepage is the only audited template that overflowed at narrow width.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container-type on reusable modules and size/content queries so modules adapt where embedded.

findings.summary: Touch targets and keyboard focus are insufficient on key controls.
findings.evidence: The control probe found many visible controls below 24px high (date tabs, links, selects); focused controls reported outline-style none.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide at least 44px touch target areas and an obvious :focus-visible indicator with sufficient contrast.

findings.summary: An unknown location search silently falls back to the Italy page.
findings.evidence: Searching for zzzzzzzzzzzzzz redirected to /Italia with no “not found” message, correction, retry, or preserved query.
findings.suggestedFix: Show a clear no-results state, preserve the query, suggest close matches, and offer retry/cancel actions.

findings.summary: Primary forecast pages miss the good LCP threshold.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured homepage LCP 4.3s and Rome forecast LCP 10.3s; the city performance score was 0.69.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP element, make it discoverable in initial HTML, prioritize it, and defer non-critical ads/scripts.

findings.summary: The load is dominated by scripts and a large third-party dependency graph.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 135 requests and 1,864,269 transferred bytes, including 40 scripts/1,134,034 bytes; Lighthouse interactive was 10.5s and flagged dependency-tree issues.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove low-value tags, load consented third parties only after need/consent, split first-party code, and strengthen caching/dependency ordering.

findings.summary: Meaningful images lack alternatives and the page landmark model is incomplete.
findings.evidence: Image probes found 3 missing alts on the homepage and 2 on the article, including the article hero; the DOM has no main landmark.
findings.suggestedFix: Add purpose-appropriate alt text (empty only when decorative) and wrap primary content in <main>.

findings.summary: Text and essential controls fail WCAG contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed color-contrast on all three Lighthouse paths; examples include the search placeholder at 2.32:1, white/orange text at 2.54:1 and date labels at 2.32:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust design tokens to meet 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text/UI, then rerun automated and visual contrast tests.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly distinguishable.
findings.evidence: The active control probe reported outline “none” and many controls have no visible focus styling; there is also no <main> landmark.
findings.suggestedFix: Add consistent :focus-visible rings, preserve logical DOM order, and add a main landmark/skip target.

findings.summary: The homepage throws an uncaught JavaScript exception.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined at the homepage inline document handler (line 3699), via jquery 3.6.3.
findings.suggestedFix: Guard the missing object, fix initialization ordering, and add an error-free smoke test for initial load.

findings.summary: Images are frequently unsized, distorted or served at unsuitable resolution.
findings.evidence: The image probe found 50/52 homepage images missing dimensions; Lighthouse failed aspect-ratio and responsive-image audits.
findings.suggestedFix: Set width/height or aspect-ratio, preserve intrinsic aspect ratios, and supply correctly sized srcset candidates.

findings.summary: The homepage requests geolocation on load and records DevTools inspector issues.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed geolocation-on-start at ilmeteo-geolocation.js line 64 and inspector-issues for analytics endpoints.
findings.suggestedFix: Request geolocation only after a user invokes “use my location”; resolve inspector/network policy issues.

findings.summary: Core transport and browser security headers are absent.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy and least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: The pre-consent privacy and tracking footprint is disproportionate.
findings.evidence: Tracker capture found 22 third-party origins and known DoubleClick, Facebook, GTM, Outbrain and Rubicon trackers; 10 cookies were present, 5 lacked Secure and several lasted 390–400 days.
findings.suggestedFix: Block non-essential trackers until valid consent, reduce vendors and retention, batch analytics, and set Secure/SameSite attributes appropriately.

findings.summary: Geolocation is requested outside user context.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse directly traced a load-time geolocation request to ilmeteo-geolocation.js line 64.
findings.suggestedFix: Move geolocation behind the clearly labelled location control and explain its purpose before invoking the API.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are not configured.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence shows no HSTS, frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy or CSP; cookie evidence also shows SameSite=None throughout.
findings.suggestedFix: Add defense-in-depth policies and narrow cookie scope/cross-site behavior to actual requirements.

findings.summary: The app manifest advertises standalone installation but no service worker is registered.
findings.evidence: The PWA probe found a standalone manifest with weather/news shortcuts and screenshots, but navigator.serviceWorker.getRegistrations() returned an empty array.
findings.suggestedFix: Register a service worker and provide a useful offline forecast/news fallback, or stop presenting the site as standalone installable.

findings.summary: Machine-readable observation time is ambiguous about time zone.
findings.evidence: Rome JSON-LD uses offsets for datePublished/dateModified but WeatherObservation.observationDate is “2026-07-27T01:10:00” with no offset or zone.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit ISO timestamps with an explicit UTC offset/IANA-zone context and keep storage unambiguous across DST.

findings.summary: Consent copy and visual hierarchy are misleading.
findings.evidence: The blocking modal headlines “NON raccogliamo dati privati” while stating data may be shared with 275 partners; the green Accept action dominates the muted reject option.
findings.suggestedFix: Use plain, accurate copy, equal visual weight for accept/reject, no pre-consent tracking, and a compact reversible preferences control.

findings.summary: Search failure is neither explained nor recoverable in context.
findings.evidence: An impossible city query silently redirects to the generic Italy forecast instead of announcing an error or offering corrected suggestions.
findings.suggestedFix: Return an accessible no-results message after submission, associate it with the search field, preserve input and offer suggestions.

findings.summary: Image delivery is wasteful for the content shown.
findings.evidence: Homepage image audit found 49 legacy-format images, 22 without srcset, 17 oversized and 29 below-fold images not lazy-loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP candidates, add sizes/srcset, lazy-load below-fold imagery and avoid duplicate hidden image instances.

findings.summary: Background and third-party work is excessive for a forecast page.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 135 requests, 40 scripts and 22 third-party origins during the short load window, while Lighthouse interactive reached 10.5s.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove redundant vendors, defer background work until idle/visible and gate analytics/ad work on consent and value.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts consume an outsized share of the page budget.
findings.evidence: Third-party evidence found 22 origins; scripts alone transferred 1.13MB and known ad/tracking vendors were active on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, remove low-value vendors and defer the remainder until user intent or consent.

taskList.title: Replace deceptive pre-consent tracking wall with honest, equal-choice consent and gate all non-essential vendors
Cut and defer script/third-party work, then fix the Rome forecast LCP
Deploy CSP, HSTS and browser defense headers; harden cookie attributes
Fix contrast, visible focus and touch-target sizing across all templates
Eliminate 360px overflow and make reusable modules container-responsive
Modernize image delivery: dimensions, aspect ratios, responsive sources, lazy loading and modern formats
Move geolocation behind explicit user intent
Provide explicit, accessible no-results recovery for location search
Complete the advertised PWA with a service worker and useful offline fallback
Add preference-driven dark/high-contrast styles and cross-document transitions
